framework_name: NIST SP 800-53 Rev. 5 — Configuration Management (CM) Family (Change Management subset)
based_on: U.S. National Institute of Standards and Technology, Special Publication 800-53 Revision 5 (a U.S. federal government publication; public domain, not copyrighted). This file includes the 7 CM-family controls most relevant to auditing a change-management process (CM-1, CM-2, CM-3, CM-4, CM-5, CM-6, CM-9) out of the full 14-control CM family. Control statements are paraphrased/condensed from the official catalog for this demo; consult NIST SP 800-53 Rev. 5 directly for the authoritative, complete text.

controls.title: Configuration Management Policy and Procedures
controls.description: The organization must develop, document, and disseminate a formal configuration/change management policy (covering purpose, scope, roles, responsibilities, and compliance) plus procedures to implement it, review and update both on a defined schedule, and designate an official responsible for maintaining them.
controls.test_procedure: Confirm a formal, written change management policy exists, names an owner/responsible role, and states a review/update cadence (not just a one-time 'last reviewed' date with no defined future cycle).

controls.title: Baseline Configuration
controls.description: The organization must develop, document, and maintain a current baseline configuration for each system (covering architecture, connectivity, and security control implementation), and review/update that baseline on a defined schedule or when components are installed/upgraded.
controls.test_procedure: Confirm the policy requires a documented, maintained baseline configuration for in-scope systems, and that changes are evaluated against that baseline rather than made ad hoc.

controls.title: Configuration Change Control
controls.description: The organization must define what types of changes require formal change control, review and explicitly approve or disapprove each proposed change (considering security/privacy impact), document the decision, implement only approved changes, retain change records for a defined retention period, and monitor change-control activity through an oversight body that convenes on a defined schedule or trigger.
controls.test_procedure: Confirm the policy defines which changes require formal review, requires an explicit approve/disapprove decision (not just a submitted ticket), documents that decision, retains records for a stated period, and routes changes through an oversight body/board rather than the requester alone.

controls.title: Impact Analyses
controls.description: The organization must analyze proposed changes to determine their potential security and privacy impact before the change is implemented.
controls.test_procedure: Confirm the policy requires a documented security/privacy impact assessment prior to approval — not merely a description of the change and its target systems.

controls.title: Access Restrictions for Change
controls.description: The organization must define, document, approve, and enforce physical and logical access restrictions on who is permitted to make changes to the system — i.e., not everyone with system access is authorized to implement changes.
controls.test_procedure: Confirm the policy restricts who may implement changes to production systems, and — critically — that the person implementing a change is not also the sole approver of that same change (segregation of duties).

controls.title: Configuration Settings
controls.description: The organization must establish and document secure configuration settings for system components (using the most restrictive setting consistent with operations), implement those settings, and formally document/approve any deviations, monitoring changes to settings against policy.
controls.test_procedure: Confirm the policy references a defined secure-configuration standard/baseline for systems, and requires any deviation from it to be documented and approved rather than left to individual discretion.

controls.title: Configuration Management Plan
controls.description: The organization must develop, document, and implement a configuration management plan addressing roles/responsibilities and CM processes, define what counts as a 'configuration item' under management, and have the plan reviewed/approved by designated personnel and protected from unauthorized disclosure or modification.
controls.test_procedure: Confirm a configuration management plan (or equivalent section within the policy) exists that assigns roles/responsibilities, defines what is under configuration control, and has a named approver.
